issues.original: A visitor decides whether to trust a small business within the first few seconds of landing on its website. The decision is mostly visual. If the page looks dated, cluttered or generic, people leave before they read a word, and no amount of clever copy gets another chance.
issues.replacement: First impressions are mostly visual. When a page looks dated, cluttered or generic, visitors have little reason to stay and read the copy, however well it is written.
issues.reason: Removes unsupported timing and universal-behaviour claims while keeping the point that visual quality affects whether copy gets read.

issues.original: The W3C's accessibility first checks ask for enough difference between text and background that people with weaker contrast sensitivity, including most people as they age, can read comfortably.
issues.replacement: The W3C's accessibility first checks ask for enough difference between text and background that people with reduced contrast sensitivity can read comfortably.
issues.reason: Removes the unsupported claim that this includes most people as they age and keeps the advice tied to the cited accessibility checks.

assessment.intent: The article gives busy owners a practical way to judge visual quality without turning design into taste alone. The answer-first structure works: look affects trust, then hierarchy, type, contrast, imagery, components and action.
assessment.specificity: Good project specificity through ABC Appliance, Okanagan Treehouse and RCCV, and the before-and-after headline rewrite is concrete. The article avoids inventing uplift claims and keeps the design advice tied to real decisions.
assessment.evidence: The evidence is appropriately light. The W3C accessibility link supports the contrast, title and alt-text checks, while Michael's live projects support the industry-specific examples. No unsupported performance percentages remain.
assessment.voice: The draft is close to Michael's voice: direct, practical, locally grounded and interested in the tradeoff between looking beautiful and helping a visitor act. It needs only the removal of a couple of broad claims, not a tonal rewrite.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. This is a strong private-review draft with enough design substance to become a durable resource. The table, checklist-style hiring guidance and one clear rewrite example give it practical value beyond a generic 'make it modern' article.
